case_name: Satish Kumar vs State Of Haryana And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Satish Kumar, father and natural guardian
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Haryana and others (including Ramesh Kumar)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's daughter Mamta Rani is missing since 4/5.3.2009 and allegedly abducted by Ramesh Kumar, who has been charged with offences under Sections 363 and 366 IPC. Petitioner seeks a writ in the nature of Habeas Corpus to recover his daughter.

legal_principles.principle: The age of the bride would be a relevant factor for consideration of initiation of action against the respondent under Section 18 of the Act or under the provisions of the Child Marriage Restraint Act.
legal_principles.held: The age of Mamta Rani would be a relevant factor for consideration of initiation of action against respondent No.4 under Section 18 of the Act or under the provisions of the Child Marriage Restraint Act and for the said purpose it would be required to establish that Mamta Rani is less than 18 years of age.
cited_cases: S. Varadarajan v. State of Madras, AIR 1965 SC 942

legal_principles.principle: The question whether the marriage between two parties is valid or not in view of a dispute in age of one party is not to be gone into in exercise of the writ jurisdiction of this Court.
legal_principles.held: The question whether the marriage between Mamta Rani (detenue) and Ramesh Kumar (respondent No.4) is valid or not in view of the dispute in age of Mamta Rani is not to be gone into in exercise of the writ jurisdiction of this Court under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India.

outcome.final_order: The petition is dismissed. The detenue has stated that she has solemnized her marriage with Ramesh Kumar (respondent No.4) of her own free will and desire, and wants to live with him.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in habeas corpus cases
